critical_steps: Two identical coordinate-axis fusion families are Parseval woven on R^2.
Intersecting both coordinate axes with span{e1+e2} gives only zero subspaces.
The source proof uses P_F P_W = P_{F intersection W}, which fails in the example.
Commutation of P_W with each source projection restores that identity and therefore preserves the original weaving bounds.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact two-dimensional, two-atom counterexample plus the standard product formula for commuting orthogonal projections.
integrity.unproved_limits: No weakest necessary-and-sufficient geometric hypothesis for intersection stability is classified.

limitations: The finding refutes arbitrary intersection with a closed subspace and supplies a clean sufficient commutation repair.
Commutation is not claimed to be necessary for every configuration.
No other theorem in the source is reassessed.

title: Intersecting a woven fusion frame with a subspace can annihilate it
